newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka arrests another opposition politician.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka arrests another opposition politician.

text.p: Sri Lankan police took another opposition politician into custody just days after arresting an influential minister in the former United National Party (UNP) government on unspecified charges, police said on Friday.
Police arrested U.L. Seneviratne, a provincial council member of the opposition UNP, late on Thursday, an official with the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) said.
Seneviratne, a close confidant of assassinated president Ranasinghe Premadasa, was taken into custody three days after Sirisena Cooray was arrested on an order given by the Defence Ministry.
Cooray, a political heavyweight in Premadasa's cabinet, was arrested on Monday and alleged to be posing a threat to national security and public peace.
"Both men are being detained under emergency regulations and being questioned. We cannot give details till investigations are completed," the CID official told Reuters.
Both men can be held for up to three months under emergency laws, which are usually used against those seen as a threat to national security.
The independent Island newspaper said both men were arrested by the same team of CID officers and on orders issued by the Defence Ministry.
On Thursday, a hearing by the Supreme Court on Cooray's arrest was postponed to Monday because the attorney general was absent, his lawyer Hemantha Warnakulasuriya said.
"It was postponed because the attorney general, though notice (to appear in court) was hand-delivered to him, was not present in court," Warnakulasuriya told Reuters.
"It is quite clear the government wants to delay the hearing to keep Mr.Cooray under arrest," he added.

Cooray, who returned to the island in April after a long stay abroad, has been ordered to appear before two presidential commissions probing poll malpractices and the killing of a senior UNP politician in 1993.
The UNP's 17 year reign ended in 1994 when the ruling People's Alliance, headed by President Chandrika Kumaratunga, won presidential and general elections.

UNP general secretary Gamini Athukorala criticised the arrest of Cooray as a misuse of emergency regulations, which he said were passed by parliament for the purpose of dealing with separatist Tamil guerrillas.
The guerrillas are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east.
